## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of LICENSE.txt.
- [x] I ran the changed-file pre-commit hooks and committed formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the applicable Python Hard Rules and test guidance.
- [ ] Maintainer action: requested labels are `cat-perf-bug`, `area:linear_attention`, and `orig-external`.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels / CuTeDSL: GDN-2 steep-decay correctness and backward correction performance on `1.31.0-rc`.

## Summary

Backport #1816 at source head `17fd57b39cfd45681637c5802ea5fe3f9c284194` to `1.31.0-rc`.
The source PR is still open. This backport can receive review and validation in parallel.
I will update this PR if #1816 changes before merging. Please coordinate final integration with #1816.

The release branch does not contain the steep-decay correction from merged PR #1644.
The first commit therefore includes the existing v1.31 adaptation of that prerequisite fix.
Its source is `d313ebe67335c31e31c241822003c6ee3d5c1c28` in `alfred-pm/cudnn-frontend`.
The following six commits backport #1816 with original author attribution and cherry-pick references.

The correctness fix preserves steep per-channel gates through bounded exact replay, with caller-owned scratch and state snapshots.
The optimization reuses overlapping gate intervals during backward correction, rather than rebuilding each interval from zero.
It retains direct token-log accumulation, nonpositive exponents, and conditional dispatch.
Lower-triangle summation order changes, so bitwise equivalence to the previous algorithm is not claimed.

## Release adaptations

The prerequisite commit adapts #1644 to the v1.31 kernel and engine interfaces.
It does not copy the develop branch or change the release version.
All 17 runtime files changed by this PR match the existing optimized v1.31 backport at `89f5a5e02e3fd665085d796d059699206c093953` byte for byte.

The #1816 runtime change, benchmark, guide, and CPU tests match its current source head byte for byte.
The shared FP64 reference is already identical on the release branch.
The only cherry-pick conflict was in `test/AGENTS.md`.
That resolution retains the release guidance and adds only the benchmark validation rules from #1816.

## Why

The v1.31 branch needs the numerical correction before it can use the interval optimization.
Including both makes this PR self-contained against the upstream release branch.
The benchmark and summary tests preserve reproducible validation, including checks that remain active under Python `-O`.

## Related issues

Related to #1644 and #1816.

## API and compatibility impact

No public API, dependency, or release-version changes.
The prerequisite correctness fix changes internal kernel arguments and increases declared caller-owned workspace for exact replay and snapshots.
Callers must continue to obtain workspace size from the prepared graph.
The optimization adds no further workspace, allocations, synchronization, or launches.
No new GPU architecture support is claimed.

## Testing

Fresh validation of exact backport commit `96e41f31e42892667bfbe228a336a17b8c6b41de` completed on one B300 (SM 10.3).
Slurm job **106241** completed with exit code zero.
JUnit reports confirm **224 passed, 0 failures, 0 errors, and 0 skips** across three separate pytest sessions:

| Suite | Passed | Scope |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Steep decay and scratch | 179 | FP64 output/gradient parity, BF16/FP16, repeatability, CUDA Graph gate transitions, state alias/rebinding, and scratch bounds |
| Existing state contracts | 12 | GDN-2 FROST overwrite and state-index cases; 4,865 unrelated cases deselected |
| Benchmark and summary | 33 | CPU validation and subprocess behavior, including Python `-O` |

Environment: Python 3.12, Torch 2.14.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, CuTe DSL 4.7.1, cuDNN backend 9.24.0, NVIDIA driver 580.173.02.

Run from `test/python` with the backport source package selected:

```text
python -m pytest -n 0 -m '' linear_attention/test_gdn2_frost_steep_decay.py linear_attention/test_gdn2_frost_steep_scratch.py -ra --junitxml=steep-scratch.xml
python -m pytest -n 0 -m '' linear_attention/test_la.py -k 'gdn2 and frost and (overwrite or state_indices)' -ra --junitxml=state.xml
python -m pytest --noconftest -c /dev/null -p no:cacheprovider -o 'markers=L0: smoke' -q linear_attention/test_gdn2_steep_decay_benchmark.py linear_attention/test_gdn2_steep_decay_summary.py --junitxml=cpu.xml
```

A validation wrapper checked every tracked Python/test file against the exact commit's SHA256 manifest before each GPU session.
It also checked every loaded `cudnn` module path after collection, including the actual helper import.
The sessions reused the existing v1.31 compiled binding.
All binding, header, and build sources match the prior qualified checkout byte for byte; this run did not rebuild C++.
Binding SHA256: `2ac18a31dab76191b44b36d6f9c8afed955e69197495067b06ff52c7888128dd`.
The helper SHA256 is `5ec675e44aa058549dd9900a203aa64d4f2ee70f1bdd648ed7789383e981a581`, matching #1816's published GPU evidence.
Full logs, JUnit reports, and provenance remain retained locally.

One graph-transition test emitted PyTorch's AccumulateGrad stream-mismatch warning. All capture/replay assertions passed.

Additional checks from the backport checkout:

```text
pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/1.31.0-rc --to-ref HEAD
# black, black-jupyter, and SPDX license header passed
# clang-format skipped: no C/C++ changes
git diff --check upstream/1.31.0-rc...HEAD
# passed
```

All changed Python files passed syntax parsing.
The 33 CPU tests also passed separately on Python 3.13 / Torch 2.14.1 before PR creation.

This is focused backport correctness coverage, not the full repository suite.
This run did not measure performance or test other GPU architectures or dependency versions.
See #1816 for its separate public B300 benchmark evidence; this PR makes no new performance claim.

@@ -25,6 +25,8 @@
 
 from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.swizzle import swizzle_xor_128b
 
+from .steep_decay import has_exact_path, steep_token_log
+
 GUARD_MARGIN = 1.0 / 32
 GUARD_QUANT_TOL_MULT = 4.0
 MACHINE_EPSILON_FP16 = 2.0**-10
@@ -40,8 +42,13 @@ def beta_guard(
     gate_prefix_ptr,
     decay_row: cutlass.Int32,
     lane_in_row_group: cutlass.Int32,
+    steep_bits,
+    log_last_ptr,
 ) -> None:
-    """Rewrite the dk_halves * 8 per-lane beta registers to beta_eff in place."""
+    """Rewrite the dk_halves * 8 per-lane beta registers to beta_eff in place.
+
+    With the steep path compiled in, ``steep_bits`` marks the lane's steep channels. Their exchange rows hold individual log2
+    gates, with the last token stored separately; the guard reads per-token decay directly."""
     dk_halves = cfg.d_k // 64
     zero = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
     one = cutlass.Float32(1.0)
@@ -66,6 +73,10 @@ def beta_guard(
                 if decay_row == 0:
                     prev_val = one
                 ratio = exp_g_frag[elem] * cute.math.rcp(prev_val, approx=True, ftz=True)
+                if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+                    if ((steep_bits >> (dim_half * 8 + f32_group * 4 + elem)) & 1) != 0:
+                        token_log = steep_token_log(cfg, gate_prefix_ptr, log_last_ptr, decay_row, f32_dim_base + elem)
+                        ratio = cute.math.exp2(token_log, fastmath=True)
                 max_ratio = cute.math.max(max_ratio, ratio)
     max_ratio = cute.math.max(max_ratio, cutlass.Float32(nvvm.shfl_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, max_ratio, 4, 31, kind=nvvm.Shfl.BFLY)))
     max_ratio = cute.math.max(max_ratio, cutlass.Float32(nvvm.shfl_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, max_ratio, 2, 31, kind=nvvm.Shfl.BFLY)))

@@ -0,0 +1,197 @@
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Numerical stages shared by all six GDN-2 chunk kernel schedules.
+
+These functions operate on one channel or row. Stage selection, shared-memory
+publication and reuse barriers remain in the calling kernel schedules.
+"""
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cutlass.experimental.primitives as nvvm
+
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.pointwise import fadd2, ffma2, fmul2, fp32_to_fp16, opaque_f32_zero, sigmoid
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.swizzle import swizzle_xor_128b
+
+from .steep_decay import exchange_offset, has_exact_path, row_operand_scales
+
+LOG2_E = 1.4426950408889634
+L2_NORM_EPS = 1.0e-6
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def gate_scale(cfg, raw_gate: cutlass.Float32) -> cutlass.Float32:
+    """Map raw gate to the log2-domain decay increment."""
+
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.safe_gate):
+        return cfg.gate_scale_log2 * sigmoid(raw_gate)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.log_gate):
+        return raw_gate * cutlass.Float32(LOG2_E)
+    return cute.math.log2(raw_gate + cutlass.Float32(1e-10), fastmath=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def scan_gate_prefixes(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, gate_raw, chunk_start, batch_seqlen, cg0_a_log_exp, cg0_dt_bias_value):
+    """Condition a channel's gates and scan in the original pairwise order.
+
+    Exact kernels retain token logs in gate_raw. The caller owns the exchange
+    stores, scan ballots and publication barriers.
+    """
+    g_prefix_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, cfg.b_t, alignment=16)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.safe_gate):
+        for row in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.b_t):
+            g_prefix_regs[row] = gate_scale(cfg, cg0_a_log_exp * (gate_raw[row] + cg0_dt_bias_value))
+    else:
+        for row in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.b_t):
+            g_prefix_regs[row] = gate_scale(cfg, gate_raw[row])
+
+    # ---- ragged tail chunk: padded rows carry no decay -----------------------
+    if chunk_start + cutlass.Int32(cfg.b_t) > batch_seqlen:
+        for row in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.b_t):
+            g_prefix_regs[row] = cutlass.Float32(0.0) if chunk_start + cutlass.Int32(row) >= batch_seqlen else g_prefix_regs[row]
+
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+        for row in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.b_t):
+            gate_raw[row] = g_prefix_regs[row]
+
+    prefix_acc = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+    for row_pair in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.b_t // 2):
+        row0 = row_pair * 2
+        row1 = row0 + 1
+        gate0 = g_prefix_regs[row0]
+        gate1 = g_prefix_regs[row1]
+        prefix0, row_pair_sum = fadd2(prefix_acc, gate0, gate0, gate1)
+        prefix1 = prefix_acc + row_pair_sum
+        g_prefix_regs[row0] = prefix0
+        g_prefix_regs[row1] = prefix1
+        prefix_acc = prefix1
+    return prefix_acc, g_prefix_regs
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def row_inverse_norm(even, odd):
+    """Reduce one row in the kernel's fixed even/odd, 4/2/1 order."""
+    total = even + odd
+    for distance in cutlass.range_constexpr(3):
+        total = total + cutlass.Float32(nvvm.shfl_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, total, 4 >> distance, 31, kind=nvvm.Shfl.BFLY))
+    return cute.math.rsqrt(total + cutlass.Float32(L2_NORM_EPS), fastmath=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def load_qk_beta_row(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, sQ_ptr, sK_ptr, sBeta_ptr, row, lane_in_row_group, opaque_one):
+    """Load raw operands, condition beta and compute row norms; Q is absent in summaries.
+
+    Each scalar sum keeps its original even/odd FFMA order. The caller publishes
+    any norms needed by other warp groups and owns the raw-stage lifetime.
+    """
+    with_q = cutlass.const_expr(sQ_ptr is not None)
+    width = cutlass.const_expr(cfg.d_k // 64 * 8)
+    raw_q_regs = None
+    if cutlass.const_expr(with_q):
+        raw_q_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    raw_k_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    raw_beta_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.l2norm):
+        k_even, k_odd = opaque_f32_zero(), opaque_f32_zero()
+        if cutlass.const_expr(with_q):
+            q_even, q_odd = opaque_f32_zero(), opaque_f32_zero()
+    for dim_half in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.d_k // 64):
+        dim_base = dim_half * 64 + lane_in_row_group * 8
+        reg_base = dim_half * 8
+        offset = dim_half * (cfg.b_t * 64) + row * 64 + swizzle_xor_128b(row, dim_base % 64, elem_bytes=2)
+        k = (sK_ptr + offset).load(count=8, alignment=16).to(cutlass.Float32)
+        beta = (sBeta_ptr + offset).load(count=8, alignment=16).to(cutlass.Float32)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(with_q):
+            q = (sQ_ptr + offset).load(count=8, alignment=16).to(cutlass.Float32)
+        for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(8):
+            raw_k_regs[reg_base + j] = k[j]
+            if cutlass.const_expr(with_q):
+                raw_q_regs[reg_base + j] = q[j]
+            value = beta[j]
+            if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.beta_sigmoid):
+                value = (sigmoid(value) * (2.0 if cfg.allow_neg_eigval else 1.0)).to(cfg.io_dtype).to(cutlass.Float32)
+            raw_beta_regs[reg_base + j] = value
+        if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.l2norm):
+            for pair in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                k_even, k_odd = ffma2(k[2 * pair], k[2 * pair + 1], k[2 * pair], k[2 * pair + 1], k_even, k_odd)
+                if cutlass.const_expr(with_q):
+                    q_even, q_odd = ffma2(q[2 * pair], q[2 * pair + 1], q[2 * pair], q[2 * pair + 1], q_even, q_odd)
+    q_norm, k_norm = opaque_one, opaque_one
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.l2norm):
+        k_norm = row_inverse_norm(k_even, k_odd)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(with_q):
+            q_norm = row_inverse_norm(q_even, q_odd)
+    return raw_q_regs, raw_k_regs, raw_beta_regs, q_norm, k_norm
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def load_operand_scales(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, row, lane_in_row_group, bits, exchange_ptr, log_last_ptr, with_restore: cutlass.Constexpr):
+    """Read all exchange data before the schedule can release its raw stage.
+
+    Backward needs decay and inverse scales only. Forward also retains the last
+    factor for K restore. Exact steep channels use bounded prefix/suffix factors.
+    """
+    width = cutlass.const_expr(cfg.d_k // 64 * 8)
+    decay_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    inverse_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    restore_regs = None
+    if cutlass.const_expr(with_restore):
+        restore_regs = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    for half in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.d_k // 64):
+        for group in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+            channel = half * 64 + lane_in_row_group * 8 + group * 4
+            values = (exchange_ptr + exchange_offset(cfg, row, channel)).load(count=4, alignment=16)
+            if cutlass.const_expr(with_restore):
+                last = (exchange_ptr + exchange_offset(cfg, cfg.b_t - 1, channel)).load(count=4, alignment=16)
+            for j in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+                index = half * 8 + group * 4 + j
+                last_value = cutlass.Float32(1.0)
+                if cutlass.const_expr(with_restore):
+                    last_value = last[j]
+                decay, inverse, restore = row_operand_scales(cfg, bits, index, row, channel + j, values[j], last_value, exchange_ptr, log_last_ptr)
+                decay_regs[index] = decay
+                inverse_regs[index] = inverse
+                if cutlass.const_expr(with_restore):
+                    restore_regs[index] = restore
+    return decay_regs, inverse_regs, restore_regs
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def key_operand_half(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, half: cutlass.Constexpr, raw_k, beta, k_norm, decay, inverse, restore):
+    """Pack the three K operands using one multiply and rounding contract.
+
+    This stage only reads registers: callers can release shared exchange storage
+    before packing, and publish each operand under its own barrier.
+    """
+    decay_pack = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, 4, alignment=16)
+    inverse_pack = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, 4, alignment=16)
+    restore_pack = None
+    if cutlass.const_expr(restore is not None):
+        restore_pack = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, 4, alignment=16)
+    for pair in cutlass.range_constexpr(4):
+        i = half * 8 + pair * 2
+        k0, k1 = fmul2(raw_k[i], raw_k[i + 1], k_norm, k_norm)
+        beta0, beta1 = fmul2(k0, k1, beta[i], beta[i + 1])
+        decay0, decay1 = fmul2(beta0, beta1, decay[i], decay[i + 1])
+        decay_pack[pair] = fp32_to_fp16(decay0, decay1, dtype=cfg.io_dtype)
+        inverse0, inverse1 = fmul2(k0, k1, inverse[i], inverse[i + 1])
+        inverse_pack[pair] = fp32_to_fp16(inverse0, inverse1, dtype=cfg.io_dtype)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(restore is not None):
+            restore0, restore1 = fmul2(inverse0, inverse1, restore[i], restore[i + 1])
+            restore_pack[pair] = fp32_to_fp16(restore0, restore1, dtype=cfg.io_dtype)
+    inverse_vec = cutlass.Vector.from_elements((inverse_pack[0], inverse_pack[1], inverse_pack[2], inverse_pack[3]), cutlass.Int32).bitcast(cfg.io_dtype)
+    decay_vec = cutlass.Vector.from_elements((decay_pack[0], decay_pack[1], decay_pack[2], decay_pack[3]), cutlass.Int32).bitcast(cfg.io_dtype)

+def query_operand_half(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, half: cutlass.Constexpr, raw_q, q_scale, decay):
+    """Pack Q decay after normalization (and the backward attention scale)."""
+    packed = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, 4, alignment=16)

+    return cutlass.Vector.from_elements((packed[0], packed[1], packed[2], packed[3]), cutlass.Int32).bitcast(cfg.io_dtype)

+"""State-gradient operands for bounded GDN-2 decay.
+
+Mild channels retain the decayed tensor-core operand. Steep channels keep the
+original FP32 gradient in caller-owned scratch and contribute through bounded
+FP32 projections. Packing the original gradient to FP16 can overflow even when
+the decayed gradient and every requested output are finite.
+
+Scratch holds one [V, K] state and a ring of [BT, K] bounded keys per persistent
+CTA. The schedules own publication and reuse: dstate_input_ready publishes the
+state, k_decay_inv_ready publishes keys, and full backward's CG2 release protects
+the state and U through the restored-key projection.
+"""
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.pointwise import fp32_to_fp16
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.swizzle import swizzle_xor_128b
+from .steep_decay import has_exact_path, steep_channel_bit
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def pack_dstate_operand(
+    cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, original, decayed, first_channel, words_ptr, steep_any, scratch_row, row_valid, width: cutlass.Constexpr[int] = 32
+):
+    """Save original steep channels in FP32 and zero their tensor-core operand."""
+    operand = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, width, alignment=16)
+    for channel in cutlass.range_constexpr(width):
+        operand[channel] = decayed[channel]
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+        if steep_any != 0:
+            steep_rows = cutlass.const_expr(cfg.d_k // len(cfg.compute_group_0_warp_ids))
+            for channel in cutlass.range_constexpr(width):
+                if steep_channel_bit(words_ptr, first_channel + channel, steep_rows) != 0:
+                    if row_valid:
+                        (scratch_row + first_channel + channel).store(original[channel])
+                    operand[channel] = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+    packed = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Int32, width // 2, alignment=16)
+    for pc in cutlass.range_constexpr(width // 2):
+        packed[pc] = fp32_to_fp16(operand[2 * pc], operand[2 * pc + 1], dtype=cfg.io_dtype)
+    return packed
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def store_steep_keys(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, raw_k, norm, decay, bits, row, lane, keys):
+    """Preserve bounded key operands before narrowing can erase a finite dU term."""
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+        for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.d_k // 64 * 8):
+            if ((bits >> i) & 1) != 0:
+                channel = (i // 8) * 64 + lane * 8 + i % 8
+                (keys + row * cfg.d_k + channel).store((raw_k[i] * norm) * decay[i])
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def add_steep_du(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, values, scratch, keys, words, value_base, lane):
+    """Add dstate @ K_restore to a 16x256b TMEM load's eight FP32 values.
+
+    The caller holds the K-operand stage until dU is published. Both operands
+    remain FP32: rounding K_restore to FP16 can erase early-token contributions
+    that become representable after multiplication by the state gradient.
+    """
+    result = cutlass.Array(cutlass.Float32, 8, alignment=16)
+    for i in cutlass.range_constexpr(8):
+        result[i] = values[i]
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+        steep_rows = cutlass.const_expr(cfg.d_k // len(cfg.compute_group_0_warp_ids))
+        # Visit only set ballot bits, in increasing channel order. A full K scan
+        # spends most of its time testing mild channels in a sparse steep tile.
+        for scan_warp in cutlass.range(len(cfg.compute_group_0_warp_ids), unroll=1):
+            remaining = (words + scan_warp).load().to(cutlass.Uint32)
+            while remaining != 0:
+                bit = cutlass.Int32(31) - cute.arch.bfind(cute.arch.brev(remaining)).to(cutlass.Int32)
+                channel = scan_warp * steep_rows + bit
+                for cs in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                    value = value_base + lane // 4 + cs * 8
+                    state = (scratch + value * cfg.d_k + channel).load()
+                    for rep in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                        for n in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                            token = lane % 4 * 2 + rep * 8 + n
+                            key = (keys + token * cfg.d_k + channel).load()
+                            i = rep * 4 + cs * 2 + n
+                            result[i] = result[i] + state * key
+                remaining = remaining & (remaining - cutlass.Uint32(1))
+    return cutlass.Vector.from_elements(tuple(result[i] for i in range(8)), cutlass.Float32)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def steep_dk_restore(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, scratch, u_ptr, channel, token, decay):
+    """Compute the steep restored-key derivative without a narrow dstate operand."""
+    total = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+    for value in cutlass.range(cfg.d_v, unroll=8):
+        state = (scratch + value * cfg.d_k + channel).load() * decay
+        offset = (value // 64) * (cfg.b_t * 64) + token * 64 + swizzle_xor_128b(token, value % 64, elem_bytes=2)
+        total = total + state * (u_ptr + offset).load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+    return total

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.

+
+"""Copy the states an aliased launch reads into scratch, so its exact twin can redo it.
+
+A ``STEEP_FAST`` launch writes its final state before its ``STEEP_EXACT`` twin runs (common/steep_decay.py).  When that
+output aliases the state the launch reads (``overwrite_initial_state``, a ``state_indices`` pool, or the backward's
+``d_initial_state`` over ``d_final_state``), the plan first copies the read state into a dense workspace snapshot and
+both launches read the copy.  ``indices`` gathers pool rows in sequence order; sequences that name the same pool row all
+read its value from before the call.  The source may have any strides with a unit innermost stride and 16-byte aligned
+``[.., v, :]`` rows, the layout the kernels' own state loads require."""
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cuda.bindings.driver as cuda
+
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.barrier import wait_on_dependent_grids
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.tma import ld_global_v4, st_global_v4
+
+USE_PDL = True
+
+BLOCK = 256
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def frost_state_snapshot(mSrc: cute.Tensor, mDst: cute.Tensor, mIdx: Optional[cute.Tensor], line_chunks: cutlass.Int64) -> None:
+    if cutlass.const_expr(USE_PDL):
+        wait_on_dependent_grids()
+    tidx, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+    bidx = cute.arch.block_idx()[0]
+    chunk = cutlass.Int64(cutlass.Int32(bidx)) * cutlass.Int64(BLOCK) + cutlass.Int64(cutlass.Int32(tidx))
+    lines = cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[0]) * cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[1]) * cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[2])
+    if chunk < lines * line_chunks:
+        line = chunk // line_chunks
+        word = chunk - line * line_chunks
+        rows_per_seq = cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[1]) * cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[2])
+        seq = line // rows_per_seq
+        rem = line - seq * rows_per_seq
+        head_wide = rem // cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[2])
+        head = head_wide.to(cutlass.Int32)
+        v_row = (rem - head_wide * cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[2])).to(cutlass.Int32)
+        slot = seq.to(cutlass.Int32)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(mIdx is not None):
+            slot = cutlass.Int32(mIdx[slot])
+        elem_bytes = cutlass.const_expr(mSrc.element_type.width // 8)
+        offset = cutlass.Int64(mSrc.layout((slot, head, v_row, 0)))
+        src = mSrc.iterator.toint() + offset * cutlass.Int64(elem_bytes) + word * cutlass.Int64(16)
+        dst = mDst.iterator.toint() + chunk * cutlass.Int64(16)
+        w0, w1, w2, w3 = ld_global_v4(src, cutlass.Int32)
+        st_global_v4(dst, (w0, w1, w2, w3), cutlass.Int32)
+
+
+frost_state_snapshot.set_name_prefix("cudnn", remove_cutlass_symbol=True)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def snapshot_states(mSrc: cute.Tensor, mDst: cute.Tensor, mIdx: Optional[cute.Tensor], stream: cuda.CUstream) -> None:
+    """``mDst[i] = mSrc[mIdx[i] if mIdx else i]`` for every row of the dense ``mDst``; issued from another kernel's host."""
+    elem_bytes = cutlass.const_expr(mSrc.element_type.width // 8)
+    line_chunks = cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[3]) * cutlass.Int64(elem_bytes) // cutlass.Int64(16)
+    total = cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[0]) * cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[1]) * cutlass.Int64(mDst.shape[2]) * line_chunks
+    grid_x = ((total + cutlass.Int64(BLOCK - 1)) // cutlass.Int64(BLOCK)).to(cutlass.Int32)
+    frost_state_snapshot(mSrc, mDst, mIdx, line_chunks).launch(grid=(grid_x, 1, 1), block=(BLOCK, 1, 1), stream=stream, use_pdl=USE_PDL)

+"""Exact intra-tile decay for steep key channels in the GDN-2 BT = 16 kernels.
+
+The chunk kernels split the intra-tile decay of key channel d between tokens t >= s,
+``2^(g[t, d] - g[s, d])`` with ``g`` the inclusive log2 gate prefix inside the 16-token
+tile, across the two operands of one register MMA: K decay / Q decay carry
+``exp2(+g[t, d])`` and K inv carries ``rcp(exp2(g[s, d]))``.  Once a prefix falls below
+-126, ``exp2(+g)`` leaves the fp32 normal range, the approximate reciprocal returns inf,
+and ``0 * inf`` turns KK, A and the state update NaN for the rest of the sequence.
+
+A channel needs exact decay when its prefix falls below the dtype threshold (``-120`` for bf16, ``-14`` for fp16),
+or its raw key magnitude makes the inverse operand unsafe. Normalized keys have magnitude at most one;
+``channel_needs_exact_decay`` also bounds unnormalized keys before selecting the path.
+
+Dispatch.  The steep path costs registers and code even where it never runs, so each kernel's ``host`` launches it
+twice (``cfg.steep_mode``):
+
+- ``STEEP_FAST``: the original arithmetic plus a range check and one ballot per scan warp; a warp that finds a steep channel stores 1 into
+  the second int32 of the kernel's scheduler slot, which the prologue zeroes every call.  A steep tile's outputs are
+  garbage at this point.
+- ``STEEP_EXACT``: launched right after, from the same host, with the steep path compiled in.  Every thread exits on
+  entry while the flag is 0, so a call without a steep tile pays one empty launch; otherwise the kernel redoes the whole
+  launch exactly (pulling tiles off the flag int, past its 1), overwriting every output before the next kernel reads it.
+  No host synchronisation is involved, so the pair is safe under CUDA graphs and ``torch.compile``.
+A launch whose output aliases a state it reads (``overwrite_initial_state``, a ``state_indices`` pool, the backward's
+``d_initial_state`` over ``d_final_state``) reads that state from a workspace snapshot (common/state_snapshot.py), so
+the exact launch never reads the fast launch's garbage.
+
+The steep path (``STEEP_EXACT``):
+
+- the gate scan retains individual log2 gates for steep channels on exchange rows ``0 .. BT - 2``;
+  the final token's log2 gate goes to a per-channel array. The last exchange row retains ``exp2(prefix)``
+  for state decay. Ballot bits select this representation, including zero gates and padding;
+- exact decay sums only the intervening token logs. Subtracting inclusive fp32 prefixes would lose small
+  gates after a large negative spike;
+- the row stage selects valid scales before constructing operands (``row_operand_scales``): K decay / Q decay use
+  ``exp2(g[t])``, which may underflow to zero harmlessly; K inv and K restore use
+  ``k[t] * exp2(g[BT - 1] - g[t])``, whose exponent is never positive;
+- ``steep_row_corrections`` adds the steep channels' exact KK and A entries, every
+  exponent ``g[t] - g[s] <= 0``, minus the products the register MMAs formed with
+  their K inv column; the register-MMA warps add the corrections to their
+  accumulators;
+- the backward picks bounded per-channel scales before it assembles gradients (``gradient_operand_scales``), so it
+  never reads token logs as prefix exponentials and repairs those lanes afterwards; ``steep_grad_corrections`` adds the
+  exact intra-tile terms;
+- ``common/gdn2_state_grad.py`` retains the steep channels' original state gradients in FP32 scratch. Their tensor-core
+  operand is zero; bounded FP32 projections supply dU, restored dK and dGate. Decay is applied before the gate dot
+  product. This avoids overflowing a finite FP32 seed or carry when it is packed into FP16.
+
+Synchronisation invariants of the steep path:
+
+- per-group scan ballots alternate between two slots where a mild tile skips the exact path's final group barrier, so
+  its next iteration can publish before every warp has read the previous ballots; the next scan's publication barrier
+  keeps a group from running two iterations ahead. Last-token and norm scratch stay behind that final barrier. The
+  ``alternating`` gate pattern covers mild/steep transitions in every scan group;
+- every correction writer arrives on the K/Q-ready barriers itself: the async-proxy fence orders only the issuing
+  thread's accesses and does not join the other lanes that wrote correction rows. ``STEEP_FAST`` keeps its original
+  elected-lane arrivals and warp-sized counts. Readers join before an elected lane releases a correction stage;
+- the exact backward's dA and dM writers both arrive on the existing diagonal-ready barrier after waiting for its slot,
+  counted directly. ``STEEP_FAST`` keeps the single-producer count because it does not consume the dM copy;
+- the public summary ops have no overwrite attribute, so their state outputs never alias and their wrappers launch
+  ``STEEP_FAST``.
+"""
+
+import dataclasses
+
+import cutlass
+import cutlass.cute as cute
+import cutlass.experimental.primitives as nvvm
+
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.pointwise import sigmoid
+from cudnn.frost.tile_dsl.swizzle import swizzle_xor_128b
+
+STEEP_LOG2_PREFIX: float = -120.0
+"""bf16 operands: a key channel whose inclusive log2 gate prefix inside a tile falls below this is steep for the tile.
+``exp2`` of the prefix reaches the fp32 (and bf16) normal floor, ``2^-126``, six binades further down."""
+
+STEEP_LOG2_PREFIX_FP16: float = -14.0
+"""fp16 operands: K inv = k * 2^-g reaches the fp16 maximum, ``65504 ~ 2^16``, two binades further down."""
+
+
+def steep_log2_prefix(io_dtype) -> float:
+    """The steep threshold for the operand dtype (a trace-time constant)."""
+    return STEEP_LOG2_PREFIX_FP16 if io_dtype == cutlass.Float16 else STEEP_LOG2_PREFIX
+
+
+STEEP_FAST: int = 0
+"""Kernel ``cfg.steep_mode``: the original arithmetic plus the steep vote; a steep tile raises the call's steep flag.
+``host`` follows the launch with a ``STEEP_EXACT`` launch of the same kernel."""
+
+STEEP_EXACT: int = 1
+"""The exact kernel of a ``STEEP_FAST`` launch: every thread exits on entry unless the flag is raised, else it redoes
+the whole launch with the steep path, pulling tiles from its own ticket."""
+
+STEEP_FLAG_SLOT: int = 1
+"""The steep flag and the exact launch's ticket share the second int32 of the kernel's scheduler slot, which the
+prologue zeroes with the first: 0 means no steep tile, and the exact launch's tickets start at the 1 the fast launch
+stored."""
+
+
+def has_exact_path(cfg) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``cfg``'s kernel compiles the steep path in (``STEEP_EXACT``; a trace-time constant)."""
+    return cfg.steep_mode != STEEP_FAST
+
+
+def steep_launch_cfg(cfg, launch_idx):
+    """Compile-time launch order: the requested specialization, then its exact twin."""
+    return cfg if launch_idx == 0 else dataclasses.replace(cfg, steep_mode=STEEP_EXACT)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def steep_exit_unless_flagged(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, flag_slot):
+    """``STEEP_EXACT`` kernel entry, after the grid-dependency wait: leave unless the fast launch raised the flag.
+
+    Do not trigger dependents here. An early trigger lets the next persistent kernel's CTAs be dispatched while this
+    grid's CTAs are still being placed, and that kernel then ran about 12% slower (B300, mild gates). Its dependents
+    launch when this grid completes, which they wait for anyway."""
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.steep_mode == STEEP_EXACT):
+        if flag_slot[STEEP_FLAG_SLOT] == cutlass.Int32(0):
+            nvvm.exit()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def steep_raise_flag(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, flag_slot, steep_word, lane_idx):
+    """``STEEP_FAST`` scan: a warp whose ballot found a steep channel raises the flag (idempotent, never read back)."""
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.steep_mode == STEEP_FAST):
+        if steep_word != 0:
+            if lane_idx == 0:
+                flag_slot[STEEP_FLAG_SLOT] = cutlass.Int32(1)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def steep_ticket(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, mScheduler):
+    """The next ticket off the scheduler slot: the first int32, or under ``STEEP_EXACT`` the flag slot past its 1."""
+    fetched = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.steep_mode == STEEP_EXACT):
+        fetched = cutlass.Int32(nvvm.atomicrmw("add", mScheduler.iterator + STEEP_FLAG_SLOT, cutlass.Int32(1), mem_order="relaxed", syncscope="gpu")) - 1
+    else:
+        fetched = cutlass.Int32(nvvm.atomicrmw("add", mScheduler.iterator, cutlass.Int32(1), mem_order="relaxed", syncscope="gpu"))
+    return fetched
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def exchange_offset(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, row, channel):
+    """Element offset of ``(row, channel)`` in one ``[BT, DK]`` fp32 gate-exchange stage."""
+    seg = channel // 32
+    return seg * (cfg.b_t * 32) + row * 32 + swizzle_xor_128b(row ^ seg, channel - seg * 32, elem_bytes=4)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def raw_offset(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, row, channel):
+    """Element offset of ``(row, channel)`` in one ``[BT, DK]`` 16-bit row-major operand tile."""
+    seg = channel // 64
+    return seg * (cfg.b_t * 64) + row * 64 + swizzle_xor_128b(row, channel - seg * 64, elem_bytes=2)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def channel_needs_exact_decay(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, prefix, raw_k_ptr, channel):
+    """Bound the inverse operand over a channel before selecting its decay path.
+
+    Normalized keys have magnitude at most one. Otherwise scan the raw tile
+    and reserve one binade below the operand maximum for reciprocal rounding.
+    The last prefix is the minimum, so this bounds every row's inverse.
+    """
+    threshold = cutlass.Float32(steep_log2_prefix(cfg.io_dtype))
+    if cutlass.const_expr(not cfg.l2norm):
+        max_key = cutlass.Float32(1.0)
+        for row in cutlass.range(cfg.b_t, unroll=1):
+            key = (raw_k_ptr + raw_offset(cfg, row, channel)).load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+            max_key = cute.math.max(max_key, cute.math.abs(key))
+        limit = cutlass.Float32(15.0 if cfg.io_dtype == cutlass.Float16 else 127.0)
+        threshold = cute.math.max(threshold, cute.math.log2(max_key) - limit)
+    return prefix < threshold
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def classify_steep_channel(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, prefix, raw_k_ptr, channel, channel_rows: cutlass.Constexpr, flag_slot, lane_idx):
+    """Classify a scan lane, mask duplicate lanes, and flag a FAST relaunch.
+
+    Callers retain ownership of stage offsets, scratch stores and barriers.
+    """
+    channel_steep = channel_needs_exact_decay(cfg, prefix, raw_k_ptr, channel)
+    word = cutlass.Int32(nvvm.vote_sync(0xFFFFFFFF, channel_steep, nvvm.VoteSync.BALLOT))
+    if cutlass.const_expr(channel_rows < cfg.threads_per_warp):
+        word = word & cutlass.Int32((1 << channel_rows) - 1)
+    steep_raise_flag(cfg, flag_slot, word, lane_idx)
+    return channel_steep, word
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def encode_gate_exchange(
+    cfg: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    prefix,
+    raw_k_ptr,
+    channel,
+    channel_rows: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    flag_slot,
+    lane_idx,
+    scan_warp,
+    token_logs,
+    values,
+    words_ptr,
+    log_last_ptr,
+    channel_active=True,
+):
+    """Classify a channel and encode its exchange registers and scan metadata.
+
+    ``values`` always holds inclusive log2 prefixes on entry. Exact steep
+    channels retain token logs except in the last row,
+    which always holds the state-decay exponential. Callers own exchange stores,
+    stage selection and publication barriers; this helper never synchronizes.
+    """
+    channel_steep, word = classify_steep_channel(cfg, prefix, raw_k_ptr, channel, channel_rows, flag_slot, lane_idx)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+        if lane_idx == 0:
+            (words_ptr + scan_warp).store(word)
+        if word != 0:
+            if channel_steep:
+                if channel_active:
+                    (log_last_ptr + channel).store(token_logs[cfg.b_t - 1])
+    for row in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.b_t):
+        values[row] = cute.math.exp2(values[row], fastmath=True)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg) and row < cfg.b_t - 1):
+            if channel_steep:
+                values[row] = token_logs[row]
+    return word
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def steep_tile_mask(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, words_ptr):
+    """Read the tile's four scan-warp ballots; FAST never reads exact-path scratch."""
+    mask = cutlass.Int32(0)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_exact_path(cfg)):
+        mask = (words_ptr.load() | (words_ptr + 1).load()) | ((words_ptr + 2).load() | (words_ptr + 3).load())
+    return mask
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def lane_steep_bits(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, words_ptr, lane_in_row_group, channel_rows: cutlass.Constexpr[int]):
+    """The steep channels a row-stage lane owns: bit ``h * 8 + j`` is channel ``h * 64 + lane_in_row_group * 8 + j``.
+
+    ``words_ptr`` holds one ballot word per scan warp; channel ``c`` is bit ``c % channel_rows`` of word
+    ``c // channel_rows``."""
+    bits = cutlass.Int32(0)

+    return cute.math.exp2(steep_interval_log(cfg, exchange_ptr, log_last_ptr, 0, row + 1, channel), fastmath=True)

+    return cute.math.exp2(steep_interval_log(cfg, exchange_ptr, log_last_ptr, row + 1, cfg.b_t, channel), fastmath=True)

+    restore = cutlass.Float32(0.0)

+def add_steep_corrections(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, acc, corr_ptr, lane_idx):
+    """Add a ``[BT, BT]`` fp32 correction tile to an m16n16 register-MMA accumulator fragment (8 values per lane)."""

+    # before that lane can let the producer overwrite the correction tile.

+    tcgen05 GEMMs read them.  With ``F(t, s) = 2^(g[t] - g[s])`` and ``K inv[s] = k_n[s] * 2^(g[BT - 1] - g[s])``

+    dq_mma = cutlass.Float32(0.0)

+    dkd_mma = cutlass.Float32(0.0)

+    for distance in cutlass.range(1, t + 1, unroll=1):

+        interval = interval + gate

+        dm = (dadm_ptr + tile + t * cfg.b_t + s).load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+        dq_attn = dq_attn + da * (k_s * decay)
+        dq_mma = dq_mma + da * k_inv_s
+        dkd_attn = dkd_attn + dm * (k_s * decay)
+        dkd_mma = dkd_mma + dm * k_inv_s
+    interval = cutlass.Float32(0.0)
+    for s in cutlass.range(t + 1, cfg.b_t, unroll=1):
+        interval = interval + steep_token_log(cfg, exchange_ptr, log_last_ptr, s, channel)
+        k_s = (raw_k_ptr + raw_offset(cfg, s, channel)).load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+        q_s = (raw_q_ptr + raw_offset(cfg, s, channel)).load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+        if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.l2norm):
+            k_s = k_s * (k_norm_ptr + s).load()

+        da = (dadm_ptr + s * cfg.b_t + t).load().to(cutlass.Float32)

+    k_t = (raw_k_ptr + raw_offset(cfg, t, channel)).load().to(cutlass.Float32)
+    if cutlass.const_expr(cfg.l2norm):
+        k_t = k_t * (k_norm_ptr + t).load()
+    beta_t = steep_beta(cfg, beta_ptr, t, channel)
+    dq_delta = scale * (dq_attn - exp_t * dq_mma)
+    dkd_delta = exp_t * dkd_mma - dkd_attn
+    return dq_delta, dk_inv, k_t * dkd_delta, beta_t * dkd_delta
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def store_steep_beta(cfg: cutlass.Constexpr, bits, beta_regs, beta_ptr, row, lane_in_row_group):
+    """Write a row's guarded beta_eff back over the raw beta tile on its steep channels, for steep_beta to read."""
+    for reg_idx in cutlass.range_constexpr(cfg.d_k // 64 * 8):
+        if ((bits >> reg_idx) & 1) != 0:
+            channel = (reg_idx // 8) * 64 + lane_in_row_group * 8 + reg_idx % 8
+            (beta_ptr + raw_offset(cfg, row, channel)).store(beta_regs[reg_idx].to(cfg.io_dtype))

+"""Compile-time storage contract for the steep-decay kernels.
+
+Offsets are bytes, lengths are elements of the region's declared type. Forward
+kernels keep separate arrays; backward kernels place these regions in bank fill.
+Stage lifetimes and synchronization remain owned by each kernel's schedule.
+"""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ScratchRegion:
+    offset: int
+    elements: int
+    nbytes: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SteepScratchLayout:
+    corr: ScratchRegion
+    dadm: ScratchRegion
+    last: ScratchRegion
+    scan: ScratchRegion
+    tile: ScratchRegion
+    norm: ScratchRegion
+    nbytes: int
+
+    def check_capacity(self, capacity: int) -> None:
+        if self.nbytes > capacity:
+            raise ValueError(f"steep scratch needs {self.nbytes} bytes, bank fill has {capacity}")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class StateGradientScratchLayout:
+    """Per-CTA global workspace: an FP32 state and a ring of bounded FP32 keys."""
+
+    state: ScratchRegion
+    keys: ScratchRegion
+    nbytes: int
+
+
+def state_gradient_scratch_layout(*, d_k: int, d_v: int, b_t: int, decay_stages: int) -> StateGradientScratchLayout:
+    state = ScratchRegion(0, d_v * d_k, d_v * d_k * 4)
+    keys = ScratchRegion(state.nbytes, decay_stages * b_t * d_k, decay_stages * b_t * d_k * 4)
+    return StateGradientScratchLayout(state, keys, state.nbytes + keys.nbytes)
+
+
+def steep_scratch_layout(
+    *,
+    b_t: int,
+    d_k: int,
+    scan_warps: int,
+    scan_stages: int,
+    last_stages: int,
+    decay_stages: int,
+    norm_stages: int,
+    dadm_stages: int = 0,
+    io_bytes: int = 2,
+) -> SteepScratchLayout:
+    """Lay out disjoint, 16-byte-aligned regions in the order used by backward."""
+    offset = 0
+
+    def region(elements, width=4):
+        nonlocal offset
+        offset = (offset + 15) // 16 * 16
+        result = ScratchRegion(offset, elements, elements * width)
+        offset += result.nbytes
+        return result
+
+    corr = region(decay_stages * 2 * b_t * b_t)
+    dadm = region(dadm_stages * 2 * b_t * b_t, io_bytes)
+    last = region(last_stages * d_k)
+    scan = region(scan_stages * scan_warps)
+    tile = region(decay_stages * scan_warps)
+    norm = region(norm_stages * b_t)
+    return SteepScratchLayout(corr, dadm, last, scan, tile, norm, (offset + 15) // 16 * 16)

+# Standalone GDN-2 steep-decay reproduction
+
+This benchmark needs one supported Blackwell GPU, PyTorch, and public cuDNN Frontend dependencies.
+It generates every input from seed 7082. It needs no model, checkpoint, dataset, application package, or distributed runtime.
+
+## Workload and checks
+
+Cases use 16 or 256 tokens, one head, key/value dimensions 64, and 0/1/64 steep channels.
+Q/K are normalized random vectors. Q/K/V and erase/write gates use BF16; log gates use FP32.
+Mild log gates are -0.02, steep gates are -6, and erase/write gates are 0.5.
+The output and all six gradients must match a CPU FP64 recurrence within 1% relative Frobenius error.
+The benchmark uses the shared `reference_gdn2.gdn2_reference` oracle.
+
+An untimed diagnostic checks the backward exact-path scheduler counter: zero for mild cases and above one for steep cases.
+It temporarily wraps internal plan methods and restores them before timing. Use this script in a single process.
+Five warmups precede 30 eager CUDA-event samples and five profiler samples of ten calls each.
+Eager intervals include host enqueue gaps. GPU busy time merges profiler intervals, excludes idle gaps, and counts overlaps once.
+Profiler overhead remains. These measurements do not establish end-to-end throughput gains.
+
+## Public environment and ABBA procedure
+
+The measured environment used `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.10-py3`, PyTorch `2.9.0a0+145a3a7bda.nv25.10`, CUDA 13.0,
+CuTeDSL 4.7.0, cuDNN 9.27.0.42, and one B300 (SM 10.3, driver 580.173.02).
+The engine requires CuTeDSL 4.7.0 even though the package metadata permits a lower version.
+Build requirements include nanobind and Ninja; install them explicitly when disabling build isolation.
+
+Start from a clean checkout of this PR. For example:
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend.git
+cd cudnn-frontend
+git fetch origin pull/1816/head
+git checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD
+docker run --rm -it --gpus device=0 --ipc=host \
+  -v "$PWD:/work" -w /work nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.10-py3 bash
+```
+
+Inside the public container, build one wheel and create two runtime copies.
+The base copy restores the helper from the exact upstream base commit.
+The compiled extension and all other runtime files therefore remain identical.
+Use a fresh output directory for each experiment:
+
+```bash
+set -euo pipefail
+unset PYTHONPATH PIP_CONSTRAINT
+REPRO_DIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/gdn2-steep.XXXXXX)
+export REPRO_DIR
+python -m venv --system-site-packages "$REPRO_DIR/venv"
+export PATH="$REPRO_DIR/venv/bin:$PATH"
+python -m pip install \
+  'nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.7.0' 'apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11' \
+  'nvidia-cudnn-cu13==9.27.0.42' 'nanobind==3.1.0' \
+  'ninja==1.11.1.1' 'cmake>=3.26' 'setuptools>=64' wheel
+export CUDNN_PATH=$(python -c 'import nvidia.cudnn; print(next(iter(nvidia.cudnn.__path__)))')
+export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$CUDNN_PATH/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"
+export CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=4
+python -m pip wheel --no-deps --no-build-isolation . -w "$REPRO_DIR/wheels"
+python -m pip install --no-deps --target "$REPRO_DIR/patch" "$REPRO_DIR"/wheels/*.whl
+cp -a "$REPRO_DIR/patch" "$REPRO_DIR/base"
+curl -fL --retry 3 \
+  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/f2aa360e5a08436651d158cfad26b05b7db5ab92/python/cudnn/linear_attention/frost/common/steep_decay.py \
+  -o "$REPRO_DIR/base/cudnn/linear_attention/frost/common/steep_decay.py"
+find "$REPRO_DIR/base" "$REPRO_DIR/patch" -name '*.pyc' -delete
+mkdir "$REPRO_DIR/results"
+python -m pip freeze > "$REPRO_DIR/results/packages.txt"
+nvidia-smi -q > "$REPRO_DIR/results/nvidia-smi.txt"
+for arm in base-A1 patch-B1 patch-B2 base-A2; do
+  case "$arm" in base-*) variant=base ;; *) variant=patch ;; esac
+  PYTHONPATH="$REPRO_DIR/$variant" python \
+    test/python/linear_attention/benchmark_gdn2_steep_decay.py \
+    --label "$arm" --output "$REPRO_DIR/results/$arm.json"
+done
+python test/python/linear_attention/summarize_gdn2_steep_decay.py "$REPRO_DIR/results"
+```
+
+Copy the result directory out before removing the container.
+If running against another kernel revision, update the pinned base and compare runtime manifests again.
+Do not use an editable installation that resolves to another checkout. Each JSON records the actual import path and helper hash.
+
+The summarizer checks identical script/reference hashes and environment identities, repeated helper hashes, all six cases, and the FP64 pass flags.
+It also checks finite errors for the output and all six gradients against the 1% tolerance.
+Timing medians must be finite and positive. Derived measurements must be finite.
+These checks remain active under optimized Python (`-O`). Both scripts write strict JSON.
+It averages the two per-arm medians for each variant. Keep all samples, including the mild controls.
+Synthetic output/gradient snapshots are saved alongside the JSON for paired numerical comparisons.
+
+## Results and evidence
+
+Measured results and qualification counts are in [PR #1816](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1816).
+The [evidence archive](https://github.com/alfredclwong/cudnn-frontend/releases/tag/evidence-pr-1816-20261023) contains raw samples, logs, JUnit reports, environment records, and the measured scripts.
+The release includes a SHA256 checksum. Generated results do not belong in this checkout.
+The archive retains the measured scripts. Later validation fixes change the benchmark script hash and require fresh ABBA records for new comparisons.
+
+## CPU validation tests
+
+The summary command needs only the Python standard library. Its regression tests need pytest and no GPU.
+The benchmark validation tests also need PyTorch. They use CPU tensors and replace GPU calls with test doubles.
+Both suites check normal and optimized Python execution.
+Run them without the GPU test harness:
+
+```bash
+python -m pytest --noconftest -c test/python/pytest.ini -o addopts= \
+  test/python/linear_attention/test_gdn2_steep_decay_summary.py \
+  test/python/linear_attention/test_gdn2_steep_decay_benchmark.py
+```
+
+## Upstream correctness tests
+
+Use the public environment above and the patched runtime. Install the public test dependencies:
+
+```bash
+python -m pip install pytest pytest-xdist looseversion
+export PYTHONPATH="$REPRO_DIR/patch"
+cd test/python
+python -m pytest -n 0 -m '' \
+  linear_attention/test_gdn2_frost_steep_decay.py \
+  linear_attention/test_gdn2_frost_steep_scratch.py -ra
+python -m pytest -n 0 -m '' linear_attention/test_la.py \
+  -k 'gdn2 and frost and (overwrite or state_indices)' -ra
+```
+
+The empty marker expression disables the default smoke-level filter.
+The linear-attention test configuration overlays this checkout's Python source onto the installed package.
+Use the exact PR checkout and verify its helper hash matches the patched runtime before testing.
+Run these commands sequentially on one GPU. Read pytest's full summary and exit status, including skips and errors.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 Alfred Wong
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Standalone synthetic GDN-2 steep-decay benchmark and FP64 check.
+
+See benchmark_gdn2_steep_decay.md for public environment setup and ABBA usage.
+The scheduler observer reads scratch only during an untimed diagnostic call.
+GPU busy time is the union of profiler intervals, not end-to-end throughput.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import contextlib
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+import cudnn
+from cudnn.linear_attention.ops.gdn2 import gated_delta_net_v2
+from cudnn.linear_attention.frost import gdn2_engine
+
+import reference_gdn2
+
+NAMES = ("q", "k", "v", "g", "b", "w")
+
+
+def inputs(tokens, steep):
+    """Create seeded inputs with the requested number of steep channels."""
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(7082)
+    shape = (tokens, 1, 64)
+    q = F.normalize(torch.randn(shape, generator=generator), dim=-1).bfloat16()
+    k = F.normalize(torch.randn(shape, generator=generator), dim=-1).bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(shape, generator=generator).bfloat16()
+    g = torch.full(shape, -0.02)
+    g[:, :, :steep] = -6.0
+    b = torch.full(shape, 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = torch.full(shape, 0.5, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    do = torch.randn(shape, generator=generator).bfloat16()
+    return [x.cuda().requires_grad_() for x in (q, k, v, g, b, w)], do.cuda()
+
+
+def reference(xs, do):
+    """Compute output and all six gradients with a CPU FP64 recurrence."""
+    refs = [x.detach().cpu().double().requires_grad_() for x in xs]
+    output, _ = reference_gdn2.gdn2_reference(*(x.unsqueeze(0) for x in refs), scale=64**-0.5)
+    output = output.squeeze(0)
+    grads = torch.autograd.grad(output, refs, do.cpu().double())
+    return [output.detach(), *(x.detach() for x in grads)]
+
+
+@contextlib.contextmanager
+def observe_schedulers(records):
+    """Record scheduler scratch during an untimed call and restore plan methods."""
+    originals = {}
+    for cls in (gdn2_engine.CompiledGdn2, gdn2_engine.CompiledGdn2Bwd):
+        original = cls.run
+        originals[cls] = original
+
+        def observed(self, views, workspace, stream, _original=original):
+            """Run the plan and read its scheduler counters before workspace release."""
+            _original(self, views, workspace, stream)
+            # Diagnostic only. Read while the caller still owns the workspace.
+            regions = dict(zip(self.carve_names, workspace.carve(self.carve)))
+            schedulers = {
+                name: torch.from_dlpack(value).cpu().tolist() for name, value in regions.items() if name.startswith("scheduler_") and name != "scheduler_all"
+            }
+            records.append({"plan": type(self).__name__, "chain": self.chain, "schedulers": schedulers})
+
+        cls.run = observed
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        for cls, original in originals.items():
+            cls.run = original
+
+
+def timed(fn, repeats=30, inner=1):
+    """Measure per-call CUDA-event latency, including host enqueue gaps."""
+    samples = []
+    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start.record()
+        for _ in range(inner):
+            fn()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end) / inner)
+    return {"median_ms": statistics.median(samples), "samples_ms": samples, "calls_per_sample": inner}
+
+
+def run_case(tokens, steep, output_dir, label):
+    """Check one case against FP64 and measure eager latency and GPU busy time."""
+    xs, do = inputs(tokens, steep)
+    offsets = torch.tensor([0, tokens], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    def call():
+        """Execute forward and backward with fixed inputs."""
+        output, _ = gated_delta_net_v2(
+            *xs,
+            offsets,
+            scale=64**-0.5,
+            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False,
+            use_beta_sigmoid_in_kernel=False,
+            allow_neg_eigval=False,
+            safe_gate=False,
+            gate_domain="log",
+            plan_name="gdn2_frost",
+        )
+        grads = torch.autograd.grad(output, xs, do)
+        return [output, *grads]
+
+    for _ in range(5):
+        call()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    records = []
+    with observe_schedulers(records):
+        result = call()
+    bwd = [r for r in records if r["plan"] == "CompiledGdn2Bwd"]
+    if not bwd:
+        raise ValueError(f"No backward scheduler records: {records}")
+    flag = bwd[-1]["schedulers"]["scheduler_bwd"][1]
+    if not ((flag > 1) if steep else (flag == 0)):
+        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected backward scheduler flag: {records}")
+    ref = reference(xs, do)
+    errors = {}
+    snapshots = {}
+    for name, actual, expected in zip(("output", *NAMES), result, ref):
+        actual = actual.detach().cpu().double()
+        if not (torch.isfinite(actual).all() and torch.isfinite(expected).all()):
+            raise ValueError(f"Non-finite {name} in output or FP64 reference")
+        relative = ((actual - expected).norm() / expected.norm().clamp_min(1e-30)).item()
+        errors[name] = {"relative_frobenius": relative, "max_abs": (actual - expected).abs().max().item()}
+        snapshots[name] = actual
+    torch.save(snapshots, output_dir / f"{label}-t{tokens}-c{steep}.pt")
+    eager = timed(call)
+    busy_samples = []
+    events = []
+    for profile_round in range(5):
+        with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CPU, torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
+            for _ in range(10):
+                call()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        gpu = [e for e in prof.events() if e.device_type == torch.autograd.DeviceType.CUDA]
+        if not gpu:
+            raise ValueError("Profiler recorded no GPU activity")
+        intervals = sorted((e.time_range.start, e.time_range.end) for e in gpu)
+        begin, end = intervals[0]
+        busy = 0.0
+        for next_begin, next_end in intervals[1:]:
+            if next_begin > end:
+                busy += end - begin
+                begin, end = next_begin, next_end
+            else:
+                end = max(end, next_end)
+        busy += end - begin
+        busy_samples.append(busy / 1000 / 10)
+        if profile_round == 0:
+            grouped = {}
+            for event in gpu:
+                entry = grouped.setdefault(event.name, {"count": 0, "total_us": 0.0})
+                entry["count"] += 1
+                entry["total_us"] += event.time_range.end - event.time_range.start
+            events = grouped
+    replay = {
+        "median_ms": statistics.median(busy_samples),
+        "samples_ms": busy_samples,
+        "calls_per_sample": 10,
+        "definition": "Union of GPU event intervals, excluding idle gaps, divided by calls",
+    }
+    row = {
+        "tokens": tokens,
+        "heads": 1,
+        "dim": 64,
+        "steep_channels": steep,
+        "scheduler_records": records,
+        "errors_fp64": errors,
+        "correct_within_one_percent": all(e["relative_frobenius"] <= 0.01 for e in errors.values()),
+        "eager": eager,
+        "gpu_busy": replay,
+        "gpu_events": events,
+    }
+    print(json.dumps({key: value for key, value in row.items() if key != "gpu_events"}, allow_nan=False), flush=True)
+    return row
+
+
+def main():
+    """Write incremental benchmark records for the six synthetic cases."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--label", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)

+    record = {

+        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+        "capability": torch.cuda.get_device_capability(),
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "cudnn_file": cudnn.__file__,
+        "cudnn_backend": cudnn.backend_version(),

+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n")

+        raise ValueError("FP64 tolerance failed; inspect saved errors")

+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Summarize all ABBA arms; refuse incomplete or mismatched runs."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import math
+import statistics
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def require(condition, message):
+    """Reject invalid benchmark records, including under optimized Python."""
+    if not condition:
+        raise ValueError(message)
+
+
+parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+parser.add_argument("results", type=Path)
+args = parser.parse_args()
+labels = ("base-A1", "patch-B1", "patch-B2", "base-A2")
+runs = {label: json.loads((args.results / f"{label}.json").read_text()) for label in labels}
+require(len({r["script_sha256"] for r in runs.values()}) == 1, "Benchmark script hashes differ")
+require(len({r["reference_sha256"] for r in runs.values()}) == 1, "FP64 reference hashes differ")
+for field in ("torch", "cuda", "dsl", "cudnn_backend", "gpu", "capability", "seed"):
+    require(len({json.dumps(r[field], allow_nan=False) for r in runs.values()}) == 1, f"Environment differs: {field}")
+for a, b in (("base-A1", "base-A2"), ("patch-B1", "patch-B2")):
+    require(runs[a]["helper_sha256"] == runs[b]["helper_sha256"], f"Helper hashes differ: {a}, {b}")
+require(runs["base-A1"]["helper_sha256"] != runs["patch-B1"]["helper_sha256"], "Base and patch helpers are identical")
+for label, run in runs.items():
+    require(run["label"] == label, f"Unexpected label in {label}")
+    require(
+        [(r["tokens"], r["steep_channels"]) for r in run["results"]] == [(t, c) for t in (16, 256) for c in (0, 1, 64)],
+        f"Incomplete or reordered cases in {label}",
+    )
+    require(all(r["correct_within_one_percent"] is True for r in run["results"]), f"FP64 check failed in {label}")
+    for case in run["results"]:
+        errors = case["errors_fp64"]
+        require(set(errors) == {"output", "q", "k", "v", "g", "b", "w"}, f"Incomplete FP64 checks in {label}")
+        for name, error in errors.items():
+            relative = error["relative_frobenius"]
+            require(math.isfinite(relative) and 0 <= relative <= 0.01, f"Invalid FP64 relative error for {name} in {label}")
+            absolute = error["max_abs"]
+            require(math.isfinite(absolute) and absolute >= 0, f"Invalid FP64 absolute error for {name} in {label}")
+rows = []
+for index in range(6):
+    cases = {label: run["results"][index] for label, run in runs.items()}
+    first = cases[labels[0]]
+    row = {"tokens": first["tokens"], "steep_channels": first["steep_channels"]}
+    for mode in ("eager", "gpu_busy"):
+        medians = {label: r[mode]["median_ms"] for label, r in cases.items()}
+        for label, median in medians.items():
+            require(math.isfinite(median) and median > 0, f"{mode} median_ms must be finite and positive in {label}, case {index}")
+        base = statistics.mean(medians[label] for label in ("base-A1", "base-A2"))
+        patch = statistics.mean(medians[label] for label in ("patch-B1", "patch-B2"))
+        speedup = base / patch
+        reduction = 100 * (1 - patch / base)
+        require(all(math.isfinite(value) for value in (base, patch, speedup, reduction)), f"Non-finite derived {mode} measurement in case {index}")
+        row[mode] = {"base_ms": base, "patch_ms": patch, "speedup": speedup, "reduction_percent": reduction, "arm_medians_ms": medians}
+    row["max_fp64_relative_error"] = max(e["relative_frobenius"] for r in cases.values() for e in r["errors_fp64"].values())
+    row["backward_scheduler_flags"] = {
+        label: [s["schedulers"]["scheduler_bwd"][1] for s in r["scheduler_records"] if s["plan"] == "CompiledGdn2Bwd"] for label, r in cases.items()
+    }
+    for flags in row["backward_scheduler_flags"].values():
+        require(flags and all(flag > 1 if first["steep_channels"] else flag == 0 for flag in flags), f"Unexpected backward scheduler flags in case {index}")
+    rows.append(row)
+summary = {
+    "results": rows,
+    "helper_hashes": {label: r["helper_sha256"] for label, r in runs.items()},
+    "script_hash": runs[labels[0]]["script_sha256"],
+    "reference_hash": runs[labels[0]]["reference_sha256"],
+}
+serialized = json.dumps(summary, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
+(args.results / "summary.json").write_text(serialized + "\n")
+print(serialized)

+def steep_gate(case, pattern):
+    """A copy of the case whose log-decay on a few key channels drops far below the 16-token-tile range the
+    exp2(g) / exp2(-g) operand split can represent (the in-tile log2 prefix below -126, i.e. a tile sum of g
+    below -87.3).  Edits are relative to each sequence start, where the kernel tiles begin."""
+    g = case.gates["g"].clone()  # [B, T, HO, K], natural log
+    if case.varlen:
+        spans = [(0, s, e) for s, e in zip(case.cu[:-1].tolist(), case.cu[1:].tolist())]
+    else:
+        spans = [(b, 0, case.T) for b in range(case.B)]
+    for b, s, e in spans:
+        seq = g[b, s:e]
+        if pattern == "steady":  # one channel at -6 per token: every full tile sums to -96
+            seq[:, 0, 7] = -6.0
+        elif pattern == "spike":  # one -200 token per tile on an otherwise mild channel: two decay clusters per tile
+            seq[5::16, 0, 3] = -200.0
+        elif pattern == "huge_spike":  # small gates after this spike must survive prefix cancellation
+            seq[:, 0, 3] = -1.0
+            seq[5::16, 0, 3] = -1.0e8
+        elif pattern == "two_spikes":  # two -150 tokens inside each tile: three clusters
+            seq[3::16, case.HO - 1, 9] = -150.0
+            seq[11::16, case.HO - 1, 9] = -150.0
+        elif pattern == "offset_window":  # a 40-token run at -6 from offset 5: partial tiles at both ends, one full tile past the edge
+            seq[5:45, 0, 11] = -6.0
+        elif pattern == "extreme":  # an effectively infinite decay and a -50 per-token decay
+            seq[:, 0, 21] = -1.0e4
+            seq[:, case.HO - 1, 33] = -50.0
+        elif pattern == "all_channels":  # every key channel of a head steep at once
+            seq[:, 0, :] = -12.0
+        elif pattern == "alternating":

+    o_ref, fs_ref = run_fwd(backend, case, initial_state=state0, output_final_state=True, batch_invariant=True)

+    separate_state = torch.empty_like(state0)
+    state = state0.clone()
+    pack = {ports[name]: t for name, t in inputs.items()}

+        assert torch.isfinite(expected_state).all(), "non-finite eager state"

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d_k", [64, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stages", [1, 2, 3])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("gradients", [False, True])
+def test_steep_scratch_regions(d_k, stages, gradients):
+    layout = steep_scratch_layout(
+        b_t=16,
+        d_k=d_k,
+        scan_warps=4,
+        scan_stages=stages,
+        last_stages=stages,
+        decay_stages=stages,
+        norm_stages=0 if gradients else 1,
+        dadm_stages=stages if gradients else 0,
+    )
+    occupied = set()
+    for field in dataclasses.fields(layout):
+        if field.name == "nbytes":
+            continue
+        region = getattr(layout, field.name)
+        assert region.offset % 16 == 0
+        assert region.offset + region.nbytes <= layout.nbytes
+        addresses = set(range(region.offset, region.offset + region.nbytes))
+        assert not occupied.intersection(addresses), field.name
+        occupied.update(addresses)
+        assert region.nbytes == region.elements * (2 if field.name == "dadm" else 4)
+    assert layout.last.elements == stages * d_k
+    assert layout.dadm.elements == (stages * 512 if gradients else 0)
+    assert layout.nbytes % 16 == 0
+    layout.check_capacity(layout.nbytes)
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="steep scratch needs"):
+        layout.check_capacity(layout.nbytes - 1)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d_k", [64, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("d_v", [64, 128])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("stages", [1, 2, 3])
+def test_state_gradient_scratch_is_disjoint(d_k, d_v, stages):
+    layout = state_gradient_scratch_layout(d_k=d_k, d_v=d_v, b_t=16, decay_stages=stages)
+    occupied = set()
+    # Model the actual producer indices across adjacent persistent CTAs.
+    for cta in range(2):
+        base = cta * layout.nbytes
+        for offset, rows in [(layout.state.offset, d_v), (layout.keys.offset, stages * 16)]:
+            assert offset % 16 == 0
+            addresses = {base + offset + (row * d_k + channel) * 4 for row in range(rows) for channel in range(d_k)}
+            assert not occupied.intersection(addresses)
+            assert max(addresses) + 4 <= base + layout.nbytes
+            occupied.update(addresses)

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 Alfred Wong
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""CPU subprocess tests for the standalone benchmark summary command."""
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.L0
+SCRIPT = Path(__file__).with_name("summarize_gdn2_steep_decay.py")
+LABELS = ("base-A1", "patch-B1", "patch-B2", "base-A2")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def runs():
+    """Create complete ABBA records with independently known timing ratios."""
+    records = {}
+    for label in LABELS:
+        median = 2.0 if label.startswith("base") else 1.0
+        records[label] = {
+            "label": label,
+            "script_sha256": "script",
+            "reference_sha256": "reference",
+            "helper_sha256": label.split("-")[0],
+            **dict.fromkeys(("torch", "cuda", "dsl", "cudnn_backend", "gpu", "capability", "seed"), "same"),
+            "results": [
+                {
+                    "tokens": tokens,
+                    "steep_channels": channels,
+                    "correct_within_one_percent": True,
+                    "errors_fp64": {name: {"relative_frobenius": 0.005, "max_abs": 0.001} for name in ("output", "q", "k", "v", "g", "b", "w")},
+                    "eager": {"median_ms": median},
+                    "gpu_busy": {"median_ms": median},
+                    "scheduler_records": [{"plan": "CompiledGdn2Bwd", "schedulers": {"scheduler_bwd": [0, 2 if channels else 0]}}],
+                }
+                for tokens in (16, 256)
+                for channels in (0, 1, 64)
+            ],
+        }
+    return records
+
+
+def summarize(tmp_path, runs, optimized=False):
+    """Execute the real CLI against four input files."""
+    for label, record in runs.items():
+        (tmp_path / f"{label}.json").write_text(json.dumps(record))
+    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, *(["-O"] if optimized else []), str(SCRIPT), str(tmp_path)], capture_output=True, text=True)
+
+
+def test_complete_summary(tmp_path, runs):
+    """Preserve valid measurements and write JSON that strict readers accept."""
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr
+    summary = json.loads((tmp_path / "summary.json").read_text(), parse_constant=lambda value: pytest.fail(f"Nonstandard JSON: {value}"))
+    assert len(summary["results"]) == 6
+    assert summary["reference_hash"] == "reference"
+    for row in summary["results"]:
+        for mode in ("eager", "gpu_busy"):
+            assert row[mode]["base_ms"] == 2.0
+            assert row[mode]["patch_ms"] == 1.0
+            assert row[mode]["speedup"] == 2.0
+            assert row[mode]["reduction_percent"] == 50.0
+        assert row["max_fp64_relative_error"] == 0.005
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("mode", ["eager", "gpu_busy"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [float("nan"), float("inf"), -float("inf"), 0.0, -1.0])
+def test_invalid_timing_does_not_replace_summary(tmp_path, runs, mode, value):
+    """Reject invalid medians before overwriting a previous summary."""
+    sentinel = tmp_path / "summary.json"
+    sentinel.write_text("previous summary\n")
+    runs["patch-B1"]["results"][0][mode]["median_ms"] = value
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert "finite and positive" in result.stderr
+    assert sentinel.read_text() == "previous summary\n"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("base,patch", [(1e308, 1e-308), (1e-308, 1e308)])
+def test_derived_overflow_is_rejected(tmp_path, runs, base, patch):
+    """Reject ratios that overflow despite finite positive inputs."""
+    for label, run in runs.items():
+        run["results"][0]["gpu_busy"]["median_ms"] = base if label.startswith("base") else patch
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert "ValueError: Non-finite derived gpu_busy measurement" in result.stderr
+    assert not (tmp_path / "summary.json").exists()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [float("nan"), float("inf"), -0.001, 0.02])
+def test_invalid_error_cannot_hide_behind_pass_flag(tmp_path, runs, value):
+    """Check each relative error independently of the saved pass flag."""
+    runs["patch-B2"]["results"][0]["errors_fp64"]["q"]["relative_frobenius"] = value
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert "ValueError: Invalid FP64 relative error for q" in result.stderr
+    assert not (tmp_path / "summary.json").exists()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("optimized", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fault", ["environment", "helper", "reference", "case", "pass_flag", "scheduler", "missing_gradient"])
+def test_validation_survives_optimized_python(tmp_path, runs, optimized, fault):
+    """Reject incomplete or mismatched records in both Python execution modes."""
+    messages = {
+        "environment": "Environment differs: torch",
+        "helper": "Helper hashes differ",
+        "reference": "FP64 reference hashes differ",
+        "case": "Incomplete or reordered cases",
+        "pass_flag": "FP64 check failed",
+        "scheduler": "Unexpected backward scheduler flags",
+        "missing_gradient": "Incomplete FP64 checks",
+    }
+    run = runs["patch-B2"]
+    if fault == "environment":
+        run["torch"] = "different"
+    elif fault == "helper":
+        run["helper_sha256"] = "different"
+    elif fault == "reference":
+        run["reference_sha256"] = "different"
+    elif fault == "case":
+        run["results"].pop()
+    elif fault == "pass_flag":
+        run["results"][0]["correct_within_one_percent"] = False
+    elif fault == "scheduler":
+        run["results"][0]["scheduler_records"] = []
+    else:
+        del run["results"][0]["errors_fp64"]["w"]
+    result = summarize(tmp_path, runs, optimized)
+    assert result.returncode != 0
+    assert f"ValueError: {messages[fault]}" in result.stderr
+    assert not (tmp_path / "summary.json").exists()
